decisions_this_run: D-064a: refuse by exclusion (`status is not PUBLISHED`) rather than by enumerating bad states. A future lifecycle state then fails closed by default instead of silently becoming enforceable.

D-064b: a retired version in a mixed set refuses the WHOLE evaluation rather than being skipped. Skipping would be the other half of the same bug - the caller would believe retired rules applied when they did not, a false audit record.
D-064c: keep the message specific (`is a draft` vs `is retired`). One means nobody published it; the other means a later release replaced it. An operator needs to know which.

D-064d: scope held to the domain predicate. The missing `approve` lifecycle verb is a real gap but needs a new transition plus persistence and audit surface; the fail-open was the higher-value fix inside one run and needed no migration.
run_summary: NEX-064 closes a latent fail-open in the policy engine. evaluate()'s docstring states rule 3 as 'Only published versions may be consulted', and the code refused a DRAFT - but it consulted a RETIRED version, so an allow rule from a superseded release still allowed. It was probed empirically before any edit: a retired allow-all version returned effect=allow. The gateway passes all_published() so no production path exploited it; the exposure is the next caller, since history() is exactly what the policy-history endpoint returns, and a caller using it would keep enforcing replaced rules. The fix is one predicate - refuse when status is not PUBLISHED - plus two regression tests, one of which asserts a retired version in a mixed set refuses the whole evaluation rather than being silently skipped. All gates green on the committed tree: ruff format and check clean, mypy clean across 140 files, 1434 passed / 4 skipped. CI then concluded 4/4 completed/success at 7456a89, so NEX-064 is VERIFIED.
